# infrawrench_slack_channel (Resource)

A Slack channel registered as an alert destination.

The **workspace connection** is not managed here: installing the Slack app is an OAuth flow a Terraform provider cannot perform. Connect the workspace once in the app, then read its `installation_id` with `data.infrawrench_slack_installations`.

Registering a channel makes it available as a destination; it does not route anything to it. What arrives here is decided by `infrawrench_alert_routing`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `channel_id` (String) Slack's own channel id, `C…` for a public channel or `G…` for a private one. Fixed at creation — pointing the registration at a different channel is a different destination, not an edit.
- `channel_name` (String) Channel name without the leading `#`. The only mutable field: it is a label, and renaming the channel in Slack does not update it here.
- `installation_id` (String) The connected Slack workspace, from `data.infrawrench_slack_installations`. Fixed at creation: a channel belongs to the workspace it lives in.

### Optional

- `is_private` (Boolean) Whether the channel is private. Fixed at creation; the update route does not carry it.

The bot must already be a member of a private channel — Slack does not let an app join one — so invite it before applying, or deliveries fail with `not_in_channel`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Infrawrench's id for this channel registration — this is the id `infrawrench_alert_routing` and `infrawrench_cost_report_notification` reference, not the Slack `C…` id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the URL when you open the object in the app, and in the
# --json output of the Infrawrench CLI.
terraform import infrawrench_slack_channel.example 5f6a7b8c-9d0e-1f2a-3b4c-5d6e7f8a9b0c
```
